title: Rates & unit conversions
examples: How do I change miles per hour to feet per second?
If I see a price in pounds and need it in dollars, what do I do?
What is the best way to remember the conversion for km/h to m/s?

explain.say: Today we learn about rates and unit conversions. A rate compares two different kinds of measurements. For example, speed is a rate.
Let us look at converting kilometers per hour to meters per second. We know one kilometer is one thousand meters. One hour is thirty six hundred seconds.
To convert, we multiply the rate by five divided by thirty six. So we multiply by five and divide by thirty six. This gives us the correct conversion factor.
Let us try an example. If something moves at seventy two kilometers per hour. We multiply seventy two by five and divide by thirty six. The answer is eight meters per second.
Next we look at currency conversion using exchange rates. An exchange rate tells you how much one money buys in another. For example, one dollar might buy zero fifty pounds.

faq.q: How do I convert kilometers per hour to meters per second?
faq.a: You multiply the speed by five and then divide the result by thirty six. This gives you the equivalent speed in meters per second.
asks: What is the formula for km/h to m/s?
Can you show me how to convert 100 km/h?

faq.a: An exchange rate is the value of one country's currency in terms of another. It changes all the time depending on the global economy.
asks: How do I know the current exchange rate?
Does the exchange rate change every day?

faq.q: Do I always multiply when converting currencies?
faq.a: No, you multiply by the rate you are given. If you are going from currency A to currency B, you multiply by the rate that tells you how much B you get for one A.
asks: Should I add or multiply for money?
If the rate is 1 to 0.8, do I multiply by 0.8?

faq.q: Is there a simple trick for km/h to m/s?
faq.a: The trick is remembering that you multiply by five and divide by thirty six. This is the consistent factor for this specific conversion.
asks: Is there a shortcut for speed units?
What is the magic number for this conversion?

faq.q: What if I am converting between two different units of length?
faq.a: You would use the standard conversion factor for those lengths. For example, you know one meter is one hundred centimeters.
asks: How do I convert feet to inches?
Do I need a formula for length units?

facts: One kilometer is equal to one thousand meters.
One hour is equal to thirty six hundred seconds.
Exchange rates show the value of one currency against another.
To convert km/h to m/s, you multiply by five divided by thirty six.

quiz.say: A car travels at 108 kilometers per hour. What is its speed in meters per second?
quiz.why: You multiply 108 by five and divide by thirty six. This gives you fifteen meters per second.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you treated it like a simple unit change without accounting for the time conversion.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you might have only divided by thirty six, forgetting to multiply by five.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you multiplied by five but forgot to divide by thirty six.

quiz.say: If the exchange rate is one euro equals one point one zero US dollars, how many dollars is three euros worth?
quiz.why: You multiply the amount in euros by the exchange rate, which is one point one zero.

wrong.1: This is wrong because you incorrectly divided the amount by the exchange rate instead of multiplying.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you only used the rate and did not multiply it by the three euros.
wrong.3: This is wrong because you might have only multiplied by one point one zero and forgotten to multiply by three.

quiz.say: A runner runs at a rate of 12 miles per hour. If one mile is one thousand meters, what is the rate in meters per hour?

options.show: One point two thousand meters per hour
options.say: One point two thousand meters per hour

options.show: Twelve divided by one thousand meters per hour
options.say: Twelve divided by one thousand meters per hour

quiz.why: Since one mile is one thousand meters, you simply multiply the number of miles by one thousand.

wrong.0: This is wrong because you only multiplied by one hundred instead of one thousand.
wrong.1: This is wrong because you treated the rate as a decimal conversion instead of a direct unit multiplication.
wrong.2: This is wrong because you divided when you should have multiplied to convert the unit of length.
